category_title: Honors students experiencing anxiety with higher-order analytical tasks
minimal_context: The student is meeting with the instructor to revise an analytical memo and practice supporting claims with qualitative data.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's review your analytical memo draft. For this next step, you need to clarify your ideas and support your claims by referencing the qualitative data.

STUDENT: Okay. I felt really confident with my writing early on in the semester, since I usually get good grades in my other classes even when I just submit a first draft. But I'm struggling to do that here.

TUTOR: Just look at your transcripts and add the quotes in. What do you have so far?

STUDENT: When I was transcribing my interview, I discovered I had not asked adequate follow-up questions. It's really making me question my competency as an interviewer to even have good data to use.

TUTOR: Well, just do your best to support your claims with the data you do have.

STUDENT: I don't think I can. I'm surprised by my own feelings of frustration and inadequacy right now, given the relative ease I experience in my other courses. Being asked to clarify these ideas with actual data is completely diminishing my confidence.

options.A: Terminate the academic demands and remove the analytical memo materials from the student for a period of 10 seconds.
options.B: Discuss strategies for engaging with the research, acknowledge and normalize the student's emotional responses, and identify sources of support.
options.C: Deliver verbal statements or physical gestures (e.g., high five, thumbs up) indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment during the meeting.
options.D: Withhold attention and do not provide a response when the student engages in problem behavior during the meeting.
